suggested_french: {REL} a de la fievre et des frissons, et pense que c'est le paludisme.
suggestion_note: HOLD LIFTED, and the reason it was held does not exist in French. The Kinyarwanda third is blocked on whether 'nkeka' -> 'akeka' is right: the transform follows the regular 1sg/3sg pattern but the speaker has not written it. French needs no transform — 'pense' is the same form for every subject. The remaining half of the question is whether attributing a SUSPICION of malaria to another person is a sensible thing for the corpus to contain at all; that is not a French question and the row carries verdict_fidelity 'unverified: clinician' rather than a lifted flag.

EX31 is the row the speaker ADDED, so it has no v1 counterpart and the builder says French must be drafted from scratch. But ex-concept-drift.md records that the rewrites rotated three concepts across three ids and that v1 EX30's concept — the runny nose — is where EX31 now sits. v1's French for EX30 is 'un nez qui coule legerement', so the v1 text for this CONCEPT exists at a different position. Used as the source, folded into an utterance to match 'amazuru arantemba gake'. PROVENANCE IS STILL A DRAFT, not v1: the string is v1's, the row it is attached to is not the row v1 attached it to.

J'ai de la fievre et ca me brule quand j'urine.
suggestion_note: HOLD LIFTED: the Kinyarwanda block was 'iyo nihagarika', unvalidated and possibly the wrong register. French has ordinary patient wording for dysuria.

suggested_french: {REL} a de la fievre et se plaint de brulures en urinant.
suggestion_note: FR-1, FOURTH SUB-CASE: a subordinate clause needs a subject pronoun, and 'quand il urine' / 'quand elle urine' forces a gender for a {REL} spanning both. English answers this with 'says it burns when they pass urine'; French cannot. Rewritten with a noun complement, 'se plaint de brulures en urinant', which needs no pronoun and is the better patient register anyway. It also keeps the reporting verb English introduced for subjective symptoms a third person cannot observe.
